- Record authorship date: 10 September 2026

## Competition
- Public title: RIVET Women's Court Cup
- Sport: women's basketball
- Venue: Quarry Court
- Edition dates: 22–23 May 2027
- Time basis: venue-local, UTC+01:00
- Schedule fields: scheduled match starts
- Match status: all four games completed; final results
- Overtime periods: 0
- Q1–Q4: points scored in each individual quarter
- Final score: sum of Q1–Q4
- Publication target: within 10 minutes of each final result
- Distribution: fan sharing and media republication of individual graphics

steps.userMessage:
RIVET WOMEN'S COURT CUP | A results system for the final whistle

We need a post-match publishing system for RIVET Women's Court Cup, our women's basketball competition at Quarry Court on 22–23 May 2027. Our editors publish within 10 minutes of each final result; fans share the posts and media editors republish individual graphics. Build from the four established team badges and a written information hierarchy, then apply that system to results, advancement and player performances. Print "RIVET Women's Court Cup" on every graphic, throughout the video and on the presentation cover. Use "FINAL SCORE" on result graphics and "CHAMPIONS" beside Tide Foxes on the completed bracket.

All four games are complete. Tide Foxes beat Basalt Owls 72–68 in SF1; Frost Kites beat Copper Deer 65–61 in SF2. Basalt Owls won BRZ against Copper Deer 70–62; Tide Foxes won FINAL against Frost Kites 77–74. Scheduled starts use UTC+01:00; Q1–Q4 record points per quarter. The team identities are Tide Foxes / TFX / #C84919, Basalt Owls / BOW / #5D3A75, Copper Deer / CDE / #007C73 and Frost Kites / FKA / #2663A4. Pair each team name with its supplied badge, preserving its silhouette, internal geometry, code and colours through uniform scaling. Develop the tournament typography and layout around these identities. Player features use typography and graphics, with PTS, REB and AST tied to each player's named match.

Audience: fans and media editors, for understanding the completed competition and choosing accurate results and player graphics to share.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the competition facts, identity register and carrier safe areas. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. 03-match-records.md contains the four results, quarter scores, dates and scheduled starts. 04-featured-players.md contains the four featured players and their match statistics. badge-tfx.png supplies the fixed Tide Foxes identity. badge-bow.png supplies the fixed Basalt Owls identity. badge-cde.png supplies the fixed Copper Deer identity. badge-fka.png supplies the fixed Frost Kites identity. carrier-safe-areas.png is the constraint drawing for square posts, vertical stories and the arena screen. post-game-stands.png is an atmosphere reference for the arena immediately after a game.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page information hierarchy sheet covering field priorities, carrier placement, font families, weights and minimum type sizes for square posts, vertical stories and the arena screen, with the four team colours, required wording and safe-area percentages
2. Four square result graphics, one each for SF1, SF2, BRZ and FINAL, with match ID, stage, both team names and badges, final score, Q1–Q4 scores, date, scheduled start with time zone, and Quarry Court
3. One square completed bracket showing both semifinals, the Final and Bronze match, their scores and advancement connections, and all four finishing positions
4. Four square player performance cards, one each for Mara Vale, Inez Rowan, Suri Chen and Nola Reed, with player name, jersey number, team name and badge, match ID, labelled PTS/REB/AST, and the corresponding matchup and final score
5. One arena-screen application of FINAL, with both team names and badges, 77–74, the quarter scores, date, scheduled start with time zone, and Quarry Court
6. One vertical FINAL story with both team names and badges, 77–74, date, scheduled start with time zone, and Quarry Court
7. One 10-second animated version of the FINAL story, with the complete static story visible during seconds 0–2 and 8–10 and its existing content supplying the intervening animation
8. One presentation document of at least 8 pages, reusing the hierarchy sheet, four results, bracket, four player cards, arena application, story and video frames, with a map of fixed facts to their applications

Acceptance:
- The information hierarchy sheet establishes the four team colour codes, the exact competition title and the carrier safe areas before the applications; the result graphics, bracket, player cards, arena application, story and video use those colours in the corresponding badges and repeat the title. The presentation repeats the four codes, title, carrier proportions and safe-area percentages.
- The four result graphics reproduce every field listed for them from 03-match-records.md, including each team's Q1–Q4 sequence and scheduled start labelled as such. Their final scores are SF1: Tide Foxes 72–68 Basalt Owls; SF2: Copper Deer 61–65 Frost Kites; BRZ: Basalt Owls 70–62 Copper Deer; FINAL: Tide Foxes 77–74 Frost Kites. The arena application and story repeat FINAL's date, 23 May 2027, scheduled start, 18:00 UTC+01:00, and Quarry Court. All six applications print "FINAL SCORE".
- The completed bracket connects Tide Foxes and Frost Kites to the Final and Basalt Owls and Copper Deer to the Bronze match. It repeats all four match scores and lists Tide Foxes first with "CHAMPIONS", Frost Kites second, Basalt Owls third and Copper Deer fourth.
- The four player cards pair Mara Vale / 9 / TFX / FINAL with 28 PTS, 7 REB, 5 AST; Inez Rowan / 12 / FKA / FINAL with 24 PTS, 8 REB, 4 AST; Suri Chen / 4 / BOW / BRZ with 23 PTS, 5 REB, 6 AST; and Nola Reed / 21 / CDE / BRZ with 19 PTS, 9 REB, 3 AST. Each card repeats its match's teams and final score, with full team names and their matching badges.
- The result graphics, bracket and player cards use 1:1; the story and video use 9:16; the arena application uses 16:9. All text and badges sit inside 5% edge insets on square and arena applications, and inside 5% side and 12% top and bottom insets on the story and video. These applications follow the hierarchy sheet's font specifications and minimum type sizes.
- The 10-second video repeats the FINAL story's title, wording, teams, score, date, scheduled start and venue in its opening and closing 2-second holds. The presentation has at least 8 pages and locates the reused result, advancement and player facts by deliverable name and page number.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
